title: The Gurmukh's learning
hookLine: true learning is reflection on the Name

cards: A cow lies in the shade long after she's finished eating, still chewing. Slowly, thoroughly, going over it again until it actually feeds her. Two days ago the Oankar asked the pandit whether he'd understood what he read.
Today it answers its own question. If reading and arguing aren't the real thing, what is? The poem's answer has a name, and a person attached to it.

teach.h: GURMUKH: FACE TURNED TO THE GURU.
teach.b: First, the person. The Gurmukh, as we've met all through these weeks, is the one whose face is turned toward the Guru. The opposite, in Gurbani, is the manmukh, the one turned toward their own mind.
Both might own the same books. What differs is the direction. Now, the learning.

In the Oankar, the Gurmukh's learning is vichar: reflection on the Name. It isn't skimming, and it isn't debating. It's going over a thing again and again, like the cow in the shade, until it feeds you.
A pandit's learning, as the poem pictures it, ends in an argument won. A Gurmukh's learning ends somewhere else, and Guru Nanak says where in a hymn in Raga Asa.

teach.h: LEARNING MAKES YOU GOOD FOR OTHERS.
teach.b: In paraphrase: when learning is reflected on, a person becomes a benefactor of others. That's a remarkable test for an education.
Not how much you know, not how well you can defend it, but whether it has made you good for the people around you. Reflection, in this teaching, doesn't keep you in your head. It sends you out.
Learning chewed long enough turns into kindness, patience, a hand offered.

Some Sikhs practice this in an ordinary way: a line from the Guru Granth Sahib read in the morning, carried and thought over through the day, and talked about with others. The goal isn't to collect lines.
It's to let one line work on you until it shows up in what you do.

how: Sikhs reflect on Gurbani through vichar: reading a hymn, hearing it explained in katha at the gurdwara, and thinking it over and discussing it with others.

o: winning debates with scholars of other paths
reflection that makes a person good for others

games.why: when learning is reflected on, a person becomes a benefactor of others. the test is outward, not a score.

practice: Take one line, from the one, or the side that bows is the heavier, or any line that matters to you, and go over it the way the cow goes over her meal: once just hearing the words, once letting a single word stand out, once letting a face come to mind, someone this line could be good for.
If your mind wanders, come back without fuss. If you pray, hold the line as a prayer; if not, let it simply be chewed.

wordCard.voice: The Gurmukh's learning. In the Oankar, real learning is vichar, reflection on the Name, and in Guru Nanak's Asa hymn, learning reflected on makes a person good for others. Today's word.

orig.note: vichar: reflection, contemplation, going over the Word in the mind.

carryVoice: Your line: reflect. Slow, repeated, and pointed outward, like the cow in the shade. Be well.

sources.ref: Asa Mahala 1 ('vidiaa veechaaree taa(n) parupkaaree'), Ang 356
